title: CDN
subtitle: Anycast edge POPs, tiered origin shielding, stale-while-revalidate caching, and dynamic edge compute.
keyTakeaways: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) terminates TLS/QUIC at hundreds of global Points of Presence (POPs) close to the user, eliminating long-haul TCP handshake RTTs and absorbing 85-99% of read traffic before it reaches the origin.
Origin Shielding funnels cache misses from hundreds of edge POPs through a single regional aggregation POP with request coalescing, preventing thundering-herd origin collapse on cache expiry.
Immutable content-addressed asset URLs (`app.8f92a.js`) paired with `stale-while-revalidate` and surrogate keys provide instant cache invalidation without origin load spikes.

sections.heading: Anycast Edge Termination, Origin Shielding & Request Coalescing
sections.body: CDNs do far more than cache static images. By advertising the same IP address from 300+ global locations via BGP Anycast, a CDN terminates the client's TCP and TLS 1.3 / HTTP/3 handshake within 10 milliseconds of the user, then reuses pre-warmed, multiplexed persistent connections over private fiber backbones to your origin.
bullets: Request Coalescing (Collapsed Forwarding): If a popular live-score JSON or video manifest expires at an Edge POP and 5,000 users request it within 20ms, the POP holds 4,999 requests in memory and sends only **1** fetch upstream.

Tiered Caching / Origin Shield: Without shielding, 300 global Edge POPs experiencing a cache miss still send 300 simultaneous requests to the origin. An Origin Shield POP sits right in front of the origin region, collapsing those 300 edge misses into a single origin request.

Dynamic API Acceleration & Edge Compute: Even for non-cacheable POST requests, edge TLS termination, TCP BBR congestion control, and Edge Workers (JWT validation, bot mitigation, A/B routing) offload heavy work from origin clusters.

codeSnippet.title: Production Cache-Control & Surrogate-Key Headers for Edge Resilience

sections.heading: Cache Key Design, Invalidation Strategies & Origin Outage Masking
sections.body: A CDN's cache hit ratio (CHR) depends on strict Cache Key normalization. Including raw query strings in random order (`?b=2&a=1` vs `?a=1&b=2`), tracking cookies, or raw `User-Agent` headers fragments the cache and drops hit ratios below 20%.
bullets: Content-Addressed Versioning vs Purging: For static bundles (JS/CSS/images), embed the SHA-256 content hash in the filename (`bundle.a1b2c3.js`) with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Never purge static assets, deploy a new HTML pointer.

Tag-Based Instant Invalidation (`Surrogate-Key` / `Cache-Tag`): For dynamic catalog or news pages, tag responses with entity IDs (`article_42`). When an editor updates the article, send a single API call to purge tag `article_42` globally in <150ms.

`stale-if-error` Origin Outage Shield: Directives like `stale-if-error=86400` instruct the CDN to continue serving slightly stale cached pages whenever the origin returns HTTP 500/502/503/504, masking backend outages from end users.

tradeOffs.pros: Maximizes cache hit ratio (99%+) and shields origin completely until data actually mutates.
tradeOffs.cons: Requires reliable CDC/webhook integration to trigger tag purges; risk of stale data if a purge webhook fails.
tradeOffs.bestFor: E-commerce product catalogs, CMS/news publishing, and media metadata APIs.

tradeOffs.pros: Zero purge infrastructure needed; automatically bounds staleness to seconds while still absorbing flash spikes.
tradeOffs.cons: Higher steady-state origin traffic for long-tail items with infrequent requests.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Live sports scores, stock tickers, flash-sale inventory counters, and high-fanout social feeds.

interviewTip: Mention **Micro-Caching** (`s-maxage=5, stale-while-revalidate=10` with Request Coalescing) in interviews: even a 5-second CDN cache on a dynamic endpoint reduces a 100,000 RPS flash-crowd spike down to 1 request every 5 seconds at your origin!
